PyTorch seeds alone do not guarantee reproducibility across releases, devices or CPU/GPU execution. Seed Python, NumPy, PyTorch and any explicit generators; disable cuDNN benchmarking and use `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` when strict determinism is required, accepting slower execution or errors for unsupported operations. [Reproducibility](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/docs/source/notes/randomness.md). Evaluation needs both `model.eval()` and `torch.inference_mode()`; inference mode disables autograd overhead but does not disable dropout or change batch-normalization behavior. Restore the previous training mode after diagnostics. [Inference mode](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.grad_mode.inference_mode.html).

DataLoader iteration can consume RNG state for worker seeds and shuffled indices. Its explicit `generator` also has separate state; workers, persistent workers, prefetching and stateful datasets introduce additional state. Consequently, restoring only main-process Python/NumPy/PyTorch CPU/CUDA RNG states cannot generally undo diagnostic loader consumption or rewind an existing sampler iterator. This is an inference from the documented loading lifecycle. Prefer a separate diagnostic loader with its own generator and isolated dataset state, or previously captured batches; seed worker libraries through `worker_init_fn`. [DataLoader documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/data.html).

Numerical comparisons should hold hardware, software, dtype, batching and execution backend fixed. Floating-point reductions can differ between mathematically equivalent batched and individual computations; bitwise equality is not generally guaranteed. Use explicit, dtype-appropriate absolute/relative tolerances and inspect maximum errors. For recommendation evaluation, also compare rankings and top-10 membership: tiny score differences near ties can change HR@10 despite numerically close outputs. [Numerical accuracy](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/docs/source/notes/numerical_accuracy.md).
